records.found: On 2026-11-04 Intellia said enrolment in its late-stage nerve-disease trial of nex-z (MAGNITUDE-2) was complete, above the 60 people planned, and on 2026-11-05 its third-quarter report said enrolment in the heart-disease trial was advancing and that it had begun giving trial doctors each patient's immune-gene (HLA) results. The release says nothing about a hold, liver safety or when results are due, and the registry's heart-trial entry (updated 2026-11-04) still shows an expected primary completion of 2027-12.

findings.what: Intellia announced completed enrolment in the late-stage MAGNITUDE-2 trial of nex-z in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with nerve disease, about 60 adults, one dose against placebo; end points at month 18 (nerve score) and day 29 (protein level).

Intellia third-quarter 2026 results: MAGNITUDE-2 enrolment finished in the quarter (above the 60-person target); enrolment in the heart trial advanced; HLA genotyping results given to investigators in the ongoing nex-z late-stage trials. No mention of a clinical hold, liver safety or filing timeline. Only regulatory date given is for a different editor, lonvo-z (PDUFA 2027-03-10).

unmatched.what: Intellia's third-quarter release says the US regulator's decision date for lonvo-z (an in-body gene editor for hereditary angioedema, not an age-related disease) is 2027-03-10 and that no advisory committee is planned. It would be the first approval of a treatment that edits a gene inside the body if granted.
unmatched.why_it_matters: It sets a date for the first regulator decision on an in-body gene editor, the tool the gene-editing entry's clinic rung needs, though that rung asks for an age-related or DNA-damage disease.
